title: Lantern and Letter
premise: In 1847, Isandro Vane, a clockmaker's apprentice hiding her identity as the daughter of a hanged rebel, is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock in the garrison town of Bellhollow. When the army requisitions the town and seizes the civil ledger containing every family's name and origin, Isandro discovers the ledger's marginalia holds coded proof of her father's innocence — and that the colonel who signed his death order now controls the last evacuation berth out of the plague-quarantined town. Forging an alliance with a disgraced army clerk and the observatory's blind astronomer, she races to expose the colonel's falsified records before the final ship sails. In the end she trades the berth — her own — for her brother's passage, and lets the restored master clock, striking the true hour, broadcast the corrected ledger to the crowd below.
about_author: Tamsin Eriksen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing requisition records and garrison correspondence from coastal towns. Her fiction is drawn to the small hands that keep institutions running and the ledgers that decide who counts.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She arrives in Bellhollow under her dead uncle's name, repairing the observatory's master clock while concealing that she is a hanged rebel's daughter. Beat: guarded competence masking fear of discovery.

chapters.title: Marginalia
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Cleaning the clock's housing, she finds a scrap of ledger paper with her father's handwriting hidden inside — coded entries she cannot yet read. Beat: the past knocking, unwelcome.

chapters.title: The Colonel's Carriage
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Colonel Harrow, who signed her father's death order, inspects the observatory and praises her work, not knowing her face. Beat: icy terror beneath a craftsman's calm.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Townsperson Maren Ostrow's POV. Soldiers nail requisition notices to every door; the civil ledger is seized from the townhouse, names and all. Beat: collective dread settling like ash.

chapters.title: The Blind Astronomer
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Astronomer Edda Sollen, who once taught Isandro's father, recognizes his handwriting in the scrap and begins teaching her the cipher. Beat: reluctant trust kindling.

chapters.title: Names Without Owners
chapters.summary: Army clerk Wren Callis's POV. Ordered to copy the seized ledger, Wren notices entries altered in the colonel's hand and quietly keeps a duplicate. Beat: a conscience choosing a side.

chapters.title: Fever at the Harbor Gate
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Quarantine is declared; ships are limited to one final berth, allocated by the colonel at his discretion. Beat: hope curdling into scarcity.

chapters.title: What the Cipher Says
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The decoded marginalia reveals her father was documenting the colonel's smuggling falsifications — the 'treason' was testimony. Beat: grief transfigured into purpose.

chapters.title: An Alliance of Thieves
chapters.summary: Isandro, Wren, and Edda meet in the observatory at night; Wren brings the duplicate ledger, Edda the cipher key. Beat: three strangers becoming conspirators.

chapters.title: The Berth List
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The colonel drafts the berth list by bribe and favor; Isandro's brother Tomas, a dockhand under a false name, is excluded. Beat: injustice made concrete and personal.

chapters.title: Tomas
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She finds Tomas and can't tell him who she is without endangering him; he begs her, as a stranger, to help his family. Beat: love constrained by secrecy.

chapters.title: The Clock Slows
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Someone sabotages the master clock; the garrison suspects the observatory and searches it, nearly finding the ledger duplicate. Beat: the walls tightening.

chapters.title: Harrow's Offer
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The colonel, needing a clockmaker, offers to place one name of her choosing on the berth list in exchange for her silence and skill. Beat: temptation with a noose in it.

chapters.title: Maren's Testimony
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren, who saw the original ledger before seizure, corroborates the altered entries to Wren. Beat: ordinary courage entering the plot.

chapters.title: The Forged Hour
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. To buy time, she repairs the clock but rigs its strike — the garrison's schedules will run on her hands. Beat: power seized, guiltily savored.

chapters.title: Wren Taken
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren is caught copying the berth list and imprisoned in the garrison cellar. Beat: the cost of conscience made flesh.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Harrow discovers the duplicate ledger's existence and offers Wren's freedom for it; Isandro must decide what the truth is worth. Beat: the moral fulcrum of the book.

chapters.title: What She Chooses
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She gives Harrow a forged duplicate, frees Wren, and learns the ship leaves at dawn — with room for one name she can still write. Beat: resolve hardened into sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At the harbor she writes Tomas's name on the list, surrendering her own passage and, with it, her anonymity — Harrow now knows whose daughter she is. Beat: the choice the blurb promised, paid in full.

chapters.title: The True Hour
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At dawn she releases the rigged strike: the master clock tolls the correct hour as Edda reads the true ledger from the observatory balcony to the assembled town. Beat: the climax — truth broadcast on time itself.

chapters.title: What the Crowd Decides
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The town, armed with the corrected names, refuses to board until Harrow is detained by his own officers; the ledger's falsifications outrank him. Beat: justice outside the law, delivered by the many.

chapters.title: Setting the Hands
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Tomas sails; Isandro stays to keep the clock and the town's records, signing her own name openly for the first time. Beat: identity claimed, quiet and whole.
